authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 2757 kaphoṇi gives Hindi kohni/kehunī, Bengali kanui and Western Pahari khunni “elbow”. Simple contracted q/k and vowel variants preserve this historical elbow family. Reviewed comparison: Chitwan kehuni “elbow” (f_rwqouaauk3wpc). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 135.1 aṅguli explicitly gives Maithili ā̃gur, Nepali aũlo and Lahnda aṅgal “finger”. The Maiya agui-type form is separately listed under 135.2 *aṅgūḍi and is assigned there; opaque reduced or retroflex-r forms remain distinct audit questions. Reviewed comparison: Goj aŋgrī “finger” (f_52rxhxmzgumkw). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10234 mūtra explicitly gives Kalasha mūtra, Bshk. mūλ and Western Pahari mūc. The survey lateral/sibilant outcomes fit the tr-cluster urine family; retroflex muṭ and ordinary mute preserve the same noun, with phonetic details left open. Reviewed comparison: Buksa mut “urine” (f_fgdpypslzzy6u). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 7733 pattra explicitly gives Lahnda pattar, Punjabi pattā and Bshk. paλ “leaf”. The l/ɬ notation in the latter and regional r-bearing or simple pata forms fit this branch; pana/pan may instead be parṇa. Reviewed comparison: KochariyaEastDanuwar pata “leaf” (f_uorip6gxmqvb2). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

Survey maśīn and macharī match those documented paradigmatic/extended forms, not the separate matsiya branch. Reviewed comparison: Rana mʌtʃʰʌli “fish” (f_v3htt7jh4gvf4). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10066 mārayati gives the mār- kill verb; maral/marla and māryo are ordinary eastern -l and western -y past/infinitive formations. Mār-diyo contains a give light verb and is not assigned as a simple inherited stem. Reviewed comparison: RathwiBareli mari “kill” (f_wzylsdq2mt5mq). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
